title: Improving the Variance of Differentially Private Randomized Experiments through Clustering
page_convention: One-based original-PDF pages; printed local pages coincide, 35 pages
scoped_summary: An exact finite counterexample disproves the advertised privacy budget for the full third-party causal-inference release. Conditional unbiasedness and possible fixed-parameter variance reductions survive this check. A separate homogeneity population identity omits design weights.

problems.title: The disclosed debiasing vector violates the advertised joint-release privacy guarantee
problems.source_claim: All information passed to the third party, including y^T Q^{-1}, is epsilon-DP under the Theorem 3.1 budget.
locations: Section 3.2, paragraph below Figure 1 and release description, PDF p. 6
suspect_steps: Replacement histogram vector sensitivity is 2/n, not the 1/n used for the first-stage Laplace privacy cost.
The noise-independent 2/gamma branch bounds randomized labels only and does not certify disclosure of the prior through the correction vector.
assumptions_verified: One public cluster contains four units, two in each treatment arm.
Binary outcomes {0,1}; neighboring observed control labels (0,0) and (1,0), with all other outcomes unchanged.
Public treatment and cluster assignments are fixed, with positive group sizes; compatible fixed potential outcomes satisfy no interference.
gamma=1/4, sigma=10 and lambda=99/100 satisfy all algorithm ranges and make Q invertible.
epsilon_tilde=log(103/99)>0 makes stated delta exactly zero.
problems.decisive_argument: For t=q_tilde(1), released y^T Q^{-1}=(-lambda*t/(1-lambda),(1-lambda*t)/(1-lambda)) reveals t. Event E={t=1/4} is equivalent up to null events to q_1=1/4 and q_0>=3/4. Its probabilities under the neighboring histograms are (1-.5*exp[-1/(2*sigma)])^2 and .25*exp[-1/sigma]. At sigma=10, log ratio 0.1952371953529369 exceeds epsilon=0.1396091380950458, with DP inequality excess 0.0148789199072658>delta=0.
problems.additional_check: At sigma=.01, lambda=.5, gamma=.25, epsilon_tilde=log 5, delta=0: claimed epsilon=8+log 5=9.6094379124 but the same observable event has log ratio 101.3862943611. Merely doubling the first branch while retaining the minimum fails.
counterevidence_checked: The target is the full advertised release, not a claim that every label-only bound is false.
Withholding the correction vector changes the release protocol and removes information explicitly required by the stated third-party estimator.
At gamma=1/K the prior is uniform and data-independent; the counterexample deliberately uses gamma<1/K.
Conditional unbiasedness is correct by Q inverse algebra; fixed-parameter variance gains are not disproved.
No actual benchmark privacy leakage or variance change was measured; published comparisons need recertification rather than presumed numerical falsity.
problems.core_dependency: Central user-level private causal inference requires the correction vector; the core privacy-variance comparison calibrates using Theorem 3.1. Its advertised budget does not cover that release.

correction.statement: Use epsilon_joint=2/sigma+epsilon_tilde and delta=max(0,1-lambda+lambda*gamma*(1-exp(epsilon_tilde))) for nonnegative epsilon_tilde, fixed public positive-size groups, sigma>0, 0<lambda<1 and 0<gamma<=1/K.
correction.proof: Product Laplace density ratio uses vector L1 sensitivity 2/n. Clip/normalize by postprocessing, then condition on fixed prior and bound the single changed categorical channel's hockey-stick excess. Adaptive composition sums epsilon. Correction vectors are functions of the released prior.
correction.limits: Does not retain the invalid 2/gamma minimum, establish optimal loss, or certify original target-budget experiments without recalibration.

problems.title: Population homogeneity identity omits sample-size and allocation weights
locations: Population interpretation at top of PDF p. 7
assumptions_verified: One fixed cluster n=n_c=4 with n_a=2.
Potential outcomes are iid Bernoulli(1/2) in the finite outcome space {0,1}.
Sample variance uses denominator n_c-1, as defined.
problems.decisive_argument: The definition gives phi_a=S^2/2. Exact expectation and all-16-vector enumeration yield E[phi_a]=1/8; the stated population quantity equals 1/4.
counterevidence_checked: For fixed design with constant treatment fractions, proportional ordering by within-cluster variance may survive.
The finite-sample phi definition remains in the variance bound; this check does not refute Theorem 3.5.
An informal proportionality reading explains the intended intuition but not the displayed equality.
problems.core_dependency: Affects exact population interpretation and normalization of homogeneity, not independently the core finite-sample variance theorem.

correction.statement: Conditional on fixed cluster sizes and treatment counts, E[phi_a]=sum_c n_c^2/(n^2*n_ac)*Var(y(a)|c). If n_ac=p_a*n_c, this is (1/(n*p_a))*sum_c(n_c/n)*Var(y(a)|c).
correction.limits: Additional random cluster-weight interpretation requires a specified sampling/design model.
